key_insight: A conformal prediction-enabled random forest prospectively reproduced clinician-recorded MS disease course labels with calibrated uncertainty, including better SPMS-related performance than Lorscheider criteria.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a potentially useful decision-support approach for harmonizing secondary progressive multiple sclerosis classification in registry-based care.
method: Trained and calibrated on Swedish MS Registry 2022 data.
Prospectively validated on an independent 2025 registry cohort not used in training.
Compared predictions against clinician labels and the Lorscheider criteria at visit and patient levels.
evidence_signal: Prospective validation showed good calibration, with per-visit accuracies of 92% for RRMS and 95% for SPMS, and individual-level sensitivity of 98% and specificity of 89%.
watch_item: The model reproduces registry clinician labels rather than a definitive biological gold standard, so implementation depends on local data quality and workflow fit.
paper_title: Prospective validation of an uncertainty-aware machine learning model for secondary progressive multiple sclerosis classification
